rate: bf16 dense tensor-core peak, fp32 accumulate

sources.label: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition product page, Specifications: 'FP16 | BF16 Tensor Core 1 PFLOP', 'FP8 Tensor Core 2 PFLOPS', 'FP4 Tensor Core 4 PFLOPS', 'TF32 Tensor Core 234 TFLOPS', 96 GB GDDR7 (the table states neither sparsity nor the accumulate width)

NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper v1.1, Appendix A, Table 4 (the Workstation Edition, the same 188-SM GB202 at a 2617 MHz boost clock): 'Peak BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' 503.8 dense / 1007.6 with the sparsity feature (footnote 2), equal to the FP16-accumulate row and half the FP8 row (1007.6 / 2015.2); 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS' 251.9 / 503.8

methodology: datasheet peak, dense, FP32 accumulate; not measured on our cards. An FMA counts as two FLOP; sparsity figures never used. The server page's 1 PFLOP FP16 | BF16 is the sparse figure (in the whitepaper's sparse ratio to its 2 PFLOPS FP8 and 4 PFLOPS FP4, as for rtx-pro-6000-server/e4m3), so the dense peak is 0.5 PFLOPS, and BF16 with FP32 accumulate runs at the FP16-accumulate rate on this professional part (whitepaper Table 4). The page's figures are rounded and its boost clock unstated: its TF32 234 TFLOPS is the whitepaper's dense 251.9 at 2431 MHz, and at the 2430 MHz maximum SM clock nvidia-smi reports on vy-nebius-1, the whitepaper's per-clock rate gives 467.8 TFLOPS. To be confirmed by a native-peak/v1 measurement
